_comment: Phase 4 sampling and validation design. Single source of truth: every script reads this file and writes the resolved values into its own output, so changing a parameter here is the only way to change the design.

inventory.note: One point per event group, not one per record: 364 usable records form 363 groups, and a group's two source records describe the same landslide.

background._comment: Presence-background (case-control) design. A background point means no mapped landslide at that location in the available inventory, NOT confirmed stable ground.
background.radius_rationale: 3.3x the largest positional uncertainty carried by any usable in-window label (30 m, measured), and wider than one 30 m analysis cell plus the immediate source area of a mapped landslide point. Costs 0.53% of district area.
background.density_rationale: Uniform sampling intensity over the eligible domain: the count follows from the area, not from the number of positives. Choosing a 1:1 or 1:3 ratio instead would tie the background size to inventory size and imply a class balance that the data do not support.

spatial_validation._comment: Fold assignment is block-based: the district is tiled into whole 3 km squares, blocks that share a single-linkage cluster (1 km, from the recorded positives) are merged into block units, and whole units are assigned to folds. A distance buffer is then applied between retained training and test points, because adjacent blocks share a boundary. Blocks are the atom of assignment, so no block is ever split across folds.
spatial_validation.block_size_rationale: Above the 1 km single-linkage scale at which the positives collapse from 363 groups to 76 clusters, so a block contains whole clusters rather than splitting them; large enough that most blocks hold several positives (73 non-empty blocks, 4.97 positives each, measured).
spatial_validation.n_folds_rationale: 363 positives over 5 folds gives ~70 test positives per fold; leave-one-block-out would leave ~1.5 positives per fold, too few to evaluate. Unequal fold sizes are accepted: the three largest clusters hold 202 of 363 positives, so even splits are arithmetically impossible.
spatial_validation.gap_rationale: 318 of 363 positives have a neighbour within 1 km. Any training point inside that distance of a test point is in the same neighbourhood the inventory resolves to, so it is dropped from training rather than allowed to leak. The same distance doubles as the single-linkage clustering threshold: one neighbourhood scale.
spatial_validation.clustering_rationale: Single-linkage distance at which 363 group-level positives collapse to 76 clusters; clusters are atomic across folds, so co-located mapped events are always evaluated together.
spatial_validation.assign_folds_by: 12 deterministic candidates (seed 20261026..20261037), each weighted k-means on merged block-unit centroids hill-climbed on fold support/positive-spread/background-spread; the best end state wins, ties at the lowest candidate
spatial_validation.min_test_positives_rationale: A fold with fewer mapped events cannot sustain a meaningful fold-level evaluation; ~12% of the inventory held out each round.
spatial_validation.min_test_clusters_rationale: A fold whose positives are one agglomeration has effectively one independent location; every fold must hold at least 5 distinct 1 km clusters.
